source_review.notes: Reviewed the official PostgreSQL buffer-manager README, PostgreSQL 18 shared-buffer and pg_buffercache documentation, MySQL 8.4 InnoDB buffer-pool and inspection documentation, SQL Server logical/physical-read and buffer-descriptor documentation, and the two cited database-systems textbooks. All seven online official/primary destinations returned HTTP 200. Pin/lock, cache-view, buffer metric, and read-path claims are scoped by engine.

evidence: Checked frame count F, page bytes P, descriptor overhead d, fixed overhead K, memory budget M, requests R, hits H, misses X, page-table T, and contextual page-tag notation.
Checked distinctions among frame/page, pin/latch/transaction lock, resident/loading/valid, logical/physical read, dirty/durable, and allocated/resident memory.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Memory and hit-rate equations are explicitly upper-bound/accounting models, not vendor sizing or latency formulas.

evidence: Recomputed the three-frame lifecycle, two A pins, B dirty state, C pinned rejection, A-to-D reuse, mappings, and counts of two hits, five miss attempts, four reads, and one blocked victim.
Recomputed the 4 GiB/8192/128/16 MiB frame example as 514092.
Recomputed the 8 GiB/16 KiB/192/64 MiB exercise bound as 514166 and raw page bytes 8424095744.
Recomputed the 99-percent example service contributions as approximately 80 seconds of misses versus 1.98 seconds of hits.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Allocator, hash, alignment, NUMA, compression, concurrency, queuing, and storage behavior remain outside the arithmetic.

evidence: Re-derived F<=floor((M-K)/(P+d)) from per-frame and fixed budget components.
Re-derived hit/miss accounting X=R-H and the limitations of H/R.
Re-derived page-table/frame uniqueness as necessary to prevent independently dirty duplicate images.
Re-derived pin temporal safety from zero-pin reuse eligibility.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The reasoning assumes correct atomic tag/state checks and does not prove a vendor's concurrent implementation.

evidence: Reviewed empty/full pools, repeated pins, underflow/leak, all-pinned/dirty/loading exhaustion, victim retag races, hash collisions, and generation reuse.
Reviewed simultaneous same-page misses, duplicate publication, waiter cancellation, owner failure, short/wrong/corrupt/authentication-failed reads, and wakeup cleanup.
Reviewed dirty eviction, WAL order, writeback failure, new-page initialization, prefetch-demand joining, unused prefetch, and crash states.
Reviewed resize, NUMA/shards, OS cache/direct I/O, memory pressure/swap, warmup, detailed-observation overhead, core-dump exposure, and storage degradation.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: No error path may publish invalid bytes, discard dirty data, or reuse a referenced frame.

evidence: Validated unique page-table keys and unique mapped frame indices.
Validated every mapping points to a valid frame with matching tag and all pins remain nonnegative.
Validated dirty B is retained, pinned C rejects D, and clean unpinned A is removed before D maps to frame 0.
The repository verifier matched exact eight-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status.
invariant_checking.notes: The model omits bytes, concurrency, loading waiters, latches, identity checks, WAL, checksums, asynchronous I/O, writeback, and replacement ranking.

evidence: Reviewed each fetch/hit/release/dirty/rejection/reuse transition and its preconditions.
Reviewed page-table/frame bijection after retagging.
Reviewed duplicate-valid-frame divergence counterexample and pin safety interval.
Reviewed memory upper-bound and hit-rate counterexample calculations.
proof_review.notes: No proof of lock freedom, fairness, replacement quality, durability, or universal cache performance is claimed.

evidence: Separated identity lifetime, content serialization, logical isolation, and I/O ownership.
Separated valid resident hits from page-table candidates and in-flight loads.
Separated dirty from committed/durable and unpinned from clean/free.
Labeled the executable load publication as a stand-in and victim choice as explicit/non-policy.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Resident, valid, unique, pinned, dirty, durable, free, hit, and physical-read claims are layer-qualified.

evidence: The standard-library buffer-frame lifecycle executed successfully through the repository verifier.
All seven online official/primary reference destinations returned HTTP 200 on 2026-08-30.
Front matter, section order, local links, ten examples, five exercises, five answers, and snippet expectations passed draft validation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live buffer pool, concurrent miss, storage I/O, checksum, WAL/writeback, replacement policy, resize, memory pressure, crash, or performance workload was executed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter consistently derives safe residency from complete identity, unique mapping, pin lifetime, content latching, validated publication, dirty protection, and defined error cleanup.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed descriptors/tags/page table, state machine, hit/miss/single-flight, pins/latches/locks, I/O validation, errors, OS cache/direct I/O, prefetch, new/dirty pages, exhaustion, sizing, sharding, warmup, security, observability, and tests.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet, executable lifecycle, ten distinct concurrency/capacity/operations examples, and five progressive exercises support self-study from frame identity through production resize diagnosis.

limitations: Internal authoring, official/primary-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and model do not certify PostgreSQL, InnoDB, SQL Server, or any live buffer pool, concurrent protocol, page identity/checksum, WAL/writeback, replacement policy, memory sizing, security posture, workload result, crash recovery, or production fitness.
